title: Groatsworth
html_source:
A groatsworth means not much. The groat was a (defunct by 1904) coin with a value of fourpence.

But the term is associated in Stephen’s mind with Shakespeare. He will use it again in his long discursus on Hamlet in the Scylla and Charybdis episode.

The reference is to Greene’s Groatsworth of Wit, a 1592 pamphlet famous for its early (and derogatory) mention of Shakespeare as an “upstart” young author.
